# Genesis Apocryphon Column 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 21 | **Condition:** Well preserved

---

**21:1** an afflicting spirit upon him and upon all the men of his household — an evil spirit.

**21:2** And it afflicted him and all the men of his house, and he could not approach her

**21:3** nor know her, though she was with him for two years.

**21:4** And at the end of two years the plagues and the afflictions grew great

**21:5** and severe upon him and upon all the men of his house.

**21:6** And he sent for all the wise men of Egypt and all the magicians

**21:7** and all the healers of Egypt, to see if they could heal him

**21:8** and the men of his house from this plague.

**21:9** But none of the healers or the magicians or any of the wise men

**21:10** could stand to heal him, for the spirit afflicted them all,

**21:11** and they fled from his presence.

**21:12** Then Harkenosh came to me and asked me to come

**21:13** and pray for the king and lay my hands upon him

**21:14** that he might live, for he had seen me in a dream.

**21:15** But Lot said to him: Abram my uncle cannot pray for the king

**21:16** while Sarai his wife is with the king. Go and tell the king

**21:17** to send away the wife of Abram to her husband, and he will pray for him

**21:18** and the king shall live.

**21:19** And when Harkenosh heard the words of Lot, he went and said to the king:

**21:20** All these plagues and these afflictions with which my lord the king

**21:21** is afflicted and stricken — they are because of Sarai, the wife of Abram.

**21:22** Restore Sarai to Abram her husband, and this plague

**21:23** and the spirit of pestilence shall depart from you.

**21:24** And the king called for Abram and said to him: What have you done to me

**21:25** regarding Sarai? You told me, She is my sister — but she is your wife!

**21:26** I took her to be my wife. Behold, your wife! Take her and go

**21:27** from all the land of Egypt. And now, pray for me and for my house

**21:28** that this evil spirit may be driven from us.

**21:29** And I prayed for him [...] and I laid my hands upon his head.

**21:30** And the plague departed from him, and the evil spirit was driven out,

**21:31** and he lived.

**21:32** And the king arose and spoke to me [...] and the king swore an oath to me

**21:33** that he had not touched her. And Sarai was brought back to me.

**21:34** And the king gave her silver and gold and much fine linen and purple.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Column 21 is well preserved. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's formal register with two adoptions from PNEUMA: "driven from/out" (21:28, 21:30) for the evil spirit's departure, replacing "rebuked." The exorcistic language of driving out a spirit is more precise than "rebuked" and better reflects the Aramaic. LOGOS's "Restore" (21:22) is preferred over PNEUMA's "Give back" for its formal weight.*
